findings: Both full guides cover existing hosted or embedded prebuilt Checkout, plus a Payment Links pointer, and paid-route Link with a `PaymentMethod.type` of `link`. Logged-in Link customers get autofill based on saved information across businesses. Enable Dashboard Link for dynamic selection and remove an existing manual `payment_method_types` list; currency limits the visible methods. The stated Setup Intents exception remains in both captures (old raw 8–37 and new raw 9–38); its manual syntax needs version qualification rather than generalizing to all setups.

The dated manual prose asks for `link` plus `card` and same-currency line items. May Node includes the list; November Ruby under the manual heading omits it. A different SDK illustration and absent request field do not revoke the prose's historical manual-list requirement or establish a Ruby API rule. Separately, 2026-09-30.endive removes writable Checkout Session-create `payment_method_types` with HTTP 400 if supplied and offers dynamic or filtered allow/exclude routes. `allowed_payment_method_types` is eligibility-filtered, and the response `payment_method_types` still represents the compatible subset (separate Checkout changelog lines 5–23). The separate Intent/SetupIntent Endive changelog lines 5–24 restricts the analogous writable parameters on specified endpoints, so do not present the Checkout guide's Setup Intents manual exception as current literal request syntax for those endpoints.

Both examples are server-side USD `payment`-mode Checkout Session requests with a success URL, without `ui_mode`. The separate November Session create reference defaults hosted_page, disallows success_url for embedded_page/elements, and conditionally requires return_url for those UIs if redirect-based methods are enabled (API lines 476–477 and 512–531). An example USD does not restrict Link globally and a success URL or sandbox OTP does not establish payment.

The two dates document no additional Checkout fees compared with other card payments. Separately the Link integrations article distinguishes type `link` and type `card` with wallet type `link`, scoped IC+ compatibility/blended rate, and immediate confirmation/settlement to Stripe balance on the same timeline as cards for successful Link payments (related raw lines 9–39). Link funding groups documentation qualifies additional funding methods and agreement-specific group fees (related raw lines 13–23 and 40–54). An underlying funding group, route availability or bank payout cannot be inferred solely from Checkout price or type wording.

Sandbox Link accounts are associated with publishable keys and should be treated as publicly available, with no real user data; any valid email can create the sandbox account, and success is any six digits except fixed invalid/expired/max attempts values. Connect uses Checkout availability for connected accounts with platform and connected-account Dashboard controls, including platform and non-platform payments on the connected account’s settings. Disable Link individually by payment method configuration and allow that propagation might take a few minutes (old lines 92–122; new 78–108).

Main route wiki/index.md line 7 → Stripe index lines 436–449 and 736 → Link concept lines 81–91 and 175. Existing source lines 19 and 27–30 and Link concept 83–89 need scoped registration/version/OTP wording, with reciprocal Checkout and domain-registration links.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-link-checkout-link-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-checkout-link-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-checkout-link.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/checkout-link`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/checkout-link, both captures describe hosted or embedded prebuilt Checkout, Link autofill for logged-in returning Link customers even across businesses, and Link-as-payment-method payments of type `link`, with pricing described as the same as other card payments (old raw lines 8-23 and new raw lines 9-24). With dynamic methods the existing Checkout integration enables Link in Dashboard and removes its manual `payment_method_types` request list. Currency restricts displayed methods, and both guides contain a manual-listing exception when collecting cards for future use with Setup Intents. The dated manual Checkout prose asks for `link` plus `card` and common-currency line items, while November’s Ruby example omits that request field (old raw lines 25-90 and new raw lines 26-76). The examples are server-side Checkout Session creation; neither creating a Session nor returning to a URL establishes payment. Separate Endive authority removes writable manual lists from Checkout Session creation. The November guide names credit cards, debit cards, and qualified U.S. bank-account purchases as supported in a nonexclusive list. May used ‘only’ with those same three funding types. Sandbox Link accounts are tied to a publishable key and should contain no real user data. For sandbox authentication, `000001` is invalid, `000002` is expired, `000003` exceeds the maximum attempts, and any other six-digit passcode authenticates successfully (old raw lines 92-105 and new raw lines 78-91). These test authentication outcomes do not prove a payment. Connect availability for connected Checkout accounts coexists with separately managed platform and connected-account settings. Dashboard disable applies individually per payment method configuration and might take a few minutes (old raw lines 92-122 and new raw lines 78-108). `source-stripe-checkout-link.md` covers the main routes but needs versioned manual and UI-specific registration language.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/checkout-link, November removes the blanket domain registration sentence and the ‘only’ funding qualifier, and replaces additional funding source ‘guarantees’ with ‘processing behavior’ while retaining same settlement timing and no integration changes (old raw lines 94-109 and new raw lines 80-95). A separate domain registration guide still identifies Link for Elements and embedded Checkout, so preserve the May sentence as dated and route the UI qualification reciprocally through `source-stripe-checkout-link.md`, Stripe Link, Checkout and domain registration. Funding availability, fee groups, successful payments settling to Stripe balance and payout to a bank are separate. cURL and Ruby replacing Node and image/table changes are presentation. The Ruby manual example omits the list despite unchanged prose (old raw lines 62-90 and new raw lines 51-76). The separate Checkout changelog documents that `2026-09-30.endive` Checkout Session create returns HTTP 400 if `payment_method_types` is passed. Dashboard-managed dynamic methods, `allowed_payment_method_types` as a request filter and `excluded_payment_method_types` are alternatives. The Session’s response `payment_method_types` reports the compatible subset. Eligibility and actual display remain distinct from the request and response lists (Checkout changelog lines 9-19). Separately, the `2026-09-30.endive` Intents changelog scopes writable-field removal to PaymentIntent create, update, and confirm and SetupIntent create and update. Those requests return HTTP 400 `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported` while their response field remains read-only (Intents changelog lines 9-16). Preserve the older manual syntax and Setup Intents wording with these version and resource qualifications. The Link integrations guide says `link` in `allowed_payment_method_types` selects the Link-as-payment-method path, with PaymentMethod type `link` even alongside `card`. Passing `card` without `link` selects the card-wallet integration, with PaymentMethod type `card` and `card.wallet.type=link` for eligible Link transactions. Neither choice guarantees display (Link integrations guide lines 9-24 and 33-39). The pinned success_url examples omit ui_mode. The separate Session create reference prohibits success_url in embedded_page or elements and conditionally requires return_url when redirect methods are enabled. No code example, test OTP, funding method label or eligibility rule demonstrates a completed payment (old raw lines 39-59 and new raw lines 40-49, old raw lines 92-109 and new raw lines 78-95).
